subject: Incident: Hosted API p99 spikes and init latency impacting FinLytics
messages:
From: Alan Brooks <alan@finlytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics SRE <sre@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T03:12:11Z
Subject: Incident: p99 spikes and 5xxs — FinLytics production — immediate help needed

Vivek,

Woke up to a production alert: since ~02:58 UTC we're seeing sustained p95/p99 latency regressions for our Hosted API traffic to your hosted model. We're also seeing a spike in 500s and gateway timeouts. Impact window started ~02:58 and we're still seeing intermittent failures.

Key symptoms:  
- p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.9s, p99 to >6s
- ~0.6% 5xx spike across the last 14 minutes
- Throughput dropped by ~30% as clients back off
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (model: redwood-alpha-3b-hosted)

Sample request ids attached in finlytics_error_summary.csv. Can you confirm whether this is a cold-start / autoscaler issue? We rely on burst capacity for peak traffic — will you be able to pre-warm or route our traffic to a warm pool? This is causing customer tickets to pile up; need an ETA for mitigation and whether an exec escalation will be opened.

Thanks,
Alan Brooks
Head of Platform — FinLytics

Attachment: finlytics_error_summary.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alan Brooks <alan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T03:25:43Z
Subject: Re: Incident: p99 spikes and 5xxs — FinLytics production — immediate help needed

Alan — thanks for the heads up and the request ids. I'm sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev 2 and have the on-call infra team looking into pool initialization behavior now.

Immediate actions I'm authorizing right now:
- Increase your reserved burst capacity by 30% for the next 2 hours to reduce cold-paths (temporary, will confirm).
- Route a subset of your traffic to a warm model variant (redwood-alpha-3b-warm) while we investigate root cause.
- Internal trace capture request: Marissa, Grace — please run a warmup trace and attach findings.

Alan, I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until we have mitigation. If you can send any additional request ids or times when you saw 5xxs that helps.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Cloud Inference — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alan Brooks <alan@finlytics.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T04:12:02Z
Subject: Re: Incident: p99 spikes and 5xxs — FinLytics production — immediate help needed

Alan / Vivek — quick technical update from infra: we captured a warmup trace for several failed cold initializations. Preliminary signals:

- Autoscaler spin-up latency is elevated due to a combination of a recent base image kernel update (deployed yesterday in a subset of pools) and node-level initialization steps delaying CUDA context warm-up. That increases first-request latency for new instances beyond our p99 SLO.
- We observed higher KV cache miss rates for the affected model shard which forces larger KV-materialization on first requests.
- The combination produces p99s in the 4–8s range for cold-paths in affected pools.

Immediate mitigations applied (visible now):
- Traffic routing to redwood-alpha-3b-warm (warm pool) for a subset of your traffic (expect ~60% of traffic routed within 5–10m).
- Temporary bump to your reserved burst instances (30% for 2 hours).

Longer-term remediation steps we're executing:
- Roll back the kernel image on affected pool nodes (starts in the next 20m).
- Add an image validation gate to prevent cross-zone kernel mismatches.
- Improve our pre-warm path and KV-materialization parallelism in the runtime.

Attached: warmup-trace-2027-04-30.json.gz (trace excerpt), redwood-playbook-pool-warmup.pdf (runbook steps we followed).

I'll follow up with a short RCA and timeline (2–4 hours).

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
Attachment: warmup-trace-2027-04-30.json.gz; redwood-playbook-pool-warmup.pdf

From: Alan Brooks <alan@finlytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics SRE <sre@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T05:01:09Z
Subject: Re: Incident: p99 spikes and 5xxs — FinLytics production — immediate help needed

Thanks Vivek/Marissa. Appreciate the fast actions. We still had a couple of customer-impacting errors around 04:40 UTC while the routing change rolled out, and this affected two enterprise customers. Given this impacted SLAs, we need clarity on financial remediation and whether this triggers executive review on your side. Please confirm the credit policy and whether an account exec will join our post-mortem.

Also please share the Jira/incident link and the timeline for the kernel rollback.

—Alan

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T08:07:21Z
Subject: Escalation: FinLytics production impact — request for exec attention and credit approval

Neha / Sean — looping you in. FinLytics (DL-4872) is seeing elevated p95/p99 and a small 5xx spike starting ~02:58 UTC. Marissa has identified a kernel-image mismatch causing slow GPU init paths; we've applied traffic routing and a temporary burst increase. They reported customer-impacting errors during the rollout window and are asking for a formal SLA credit and exec representation in the post-mortem.

Request:
- Approve an interim invoice credit (customer requests a visible remedy; suggest 10% for impacted billing period while we complete RCA).
- Exec reps to attend the post-mortem scheduled after mitigation (proposed: today 17:00 UTC).
- Priority for the kernel rollback and follow-up validation (Marissa has schedule ~20m to start rollback).

Full thread below for context.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Cloud Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alan Brooks <alan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T12:45:02Z
Subject: Re: Incident: p99 spikes and 5xxs — FinLytics production — immediate help needed

Alan — I'm very sorry for the disruption. Thank you for the clear signal and the traces you provided. We value FinLytics as a strategic customer and want to make this right.

What we're committing to now:
- Hotfix: kernel rollback started at ~08:30 UTC and completed for the majority of impacted pools by 09:05 UTC. We've validated p99 returned to baseline for routed traffic. Full validation ongoing.
- Credit: we'll issue a 10% credit on the affected billing period as an interim measure; final credit to be confirmed after RCA.
- Post-mortem: Marissa will produce an RCA doc; we propose a joint post-mortem at 17:00 UTC today. We'll include a timeline, fixes delivered, and follow-up action items.
- Support: our SRE team (Marissa & Grace) can join your on-call for a two-hour burn to triage remaining anomalies.

I've opened JIRA SUP-7894 and shared an incident doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxy-example-incident-doc. HubSpot ticket hs_record_546732 has been linked.

If you'd like a short call now, I can be available. Otherwise we will proceed with the post-mortem and send the interim credit confirmation by COB.

—Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
